assignments.brief_reason: Uses harsh/profane tone/outlandishness as a moderation basis to reject keep opinions when it becomes profane.
Removes when posts add no conversational value, fitting a general removal-by-standards approach for keeping non-toxic opinions.
“Professionalism standard” isn’t explicitly a threat/toxicity rule or a free-speech-with-violence exception.
Threatening/vicious tone and major cussing drive removal, aligning with keeping speech except violence/threats and closely related bad language.
Explicitly applies the same moderation standard to both sides to avoid viewpoint bias, with tone/target sub-rules.
Clear profanity threshold (reject if cursing/foul language) while allowing if civil, consistent with violence/threat exceptions plus bad-language boundary.
Rejects angry/cursing/name-calling but allows opinions/questions without strict name-calling—tone/toxicity boundary under speech-allowing approach.
Removes personal/side attacks rather than information, which functions like a toxicity/threatening/insult removal standard.
Free-speech absolutism with removal primarily for attacking or unthoughtful reactions; closest match to keeping most speech with exceptions.
Anti-censorship removal only for bad grammar/syntax/insult behavior doesn’t align cleanly with violence/threat or specific toxicity criteria in the themes.
Allows most speech but draws a line for vulgarity made purely to be vulgar—exception-based tolerance.
Removes based on plausibility/falsehood that could harm readers via perspective-taking, not primarily threat/toxicity or violence exceptions.
Separates “true viewpoint” vs “nonsense” for both sides—content-quality discrimination not covered by threat/toxicity themes.
Keeps unless content explicitly incites violence or is very profane—directly matches violence/threat exceptions with bad-language constraint.
Removal rule is factual inaccuracy/misinformation, which isn’t specified in the threat/toxicity or free-speech-with-violence themes.
Critiques the approach due to misinformation/extreme tradeoffs; doesn’t map to the moderation standard/tone rules in themes.
Respectful vs insulting personal attack guides allow/remove, fitting a toxicity/insult-based removal standard.
Keeps mostly civil but removes when it seems like complete rumors—operates as a removal standard tied to harmful/low-quality content.
Focuses on argument construction/validity and quality rather than threat/toxicity or profanity thresholds.
Notes political affiliation and wording affected decisions—affect/confidence factor not covered by the provided moderation standard themes.
